findings.text: The condition calls `Error(t, panicErr)` and `EqualError(t, panicErr, errString)`, and both report failures on `t` themselves. With `panic(errors.New("a"))` and expected string "b", `EqualError` fails first and then `Fail` fires again, so one mismatch gives two or more failure reports. The check should be a plain `panicErr.Error() != errString` comparison, which reports once.
